The child expands this same sequence with Justice Reed-specific detail. C15 and C12 share the broader resignation-acceptance and service-appreciation structure, but are less specifically aligned.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"My dear Mr. Justice: I am most appreciative of your courtesy in giving me advance notice of your intention to retire from active service","parent_excerpt":"Dear Mr. Justice: Thank you very much for giving me timely notice that, because of your health, you will retire","explanation":"Distinctively parallel salutation and opening acknowledgment of advance notice from a retiring Supreme Court Justice."},{"child_excerpt":"I seize the opportunity to tender my congratulations on your long and splendid record in public service","parent_excerpt":"May I be permitted to express my appreciation of the many years you have given to public service on the Federal Bench, culminating in your service on the Supreme Court?","explanation":"Both next commend the Justice's lengthy public and judicial service, specifically including the Supreme Court."},{"child_excerpt":"there lie ahead of you long happiness and satisfaction as well as opportunity to continue to contribute","parent_excerpt":"I trust you will find your life in retirement to be filled both with contentment and good health.","explanation":"Both conclude the substantive message with wishes for a happy and satisfying retirement."},{"child_excerpt":"With my greetings to Mrs. Reed and warm regard to yourself","parent_excerpt":"With personal regard","explanation":"Closely parallel personal-regard closing, though this element alone is conventional."}]}
